title: Function tables: In / Out tables ruled by a rule (`function-table`)

template.also: js/modules/gen-function-table.js deals the item (every option read there); js/modules/sheet/providers/function-table.js supplies strings, worked steps, wrong answers and misconceptions; screen-cell.js draws the same cell on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz (one input per slot, checked by ftAnswerMatches)

summary: One kit cell, five tasks: an In / Out table under a black-and-white function machine (In -> [rule] -> Out). Use the rule (write each Out), find the rule (every row printed; the pupil writes the sign and the number IN the machine's box where it fits a third of the page, else in the frame under the table), work the rule backward (write each In), mixed blanks, or make your own table. A Check row can follow any task but make. function_table_easy defaults to one + / - step with numbers to 20, four rows in order, filling the Out column; function_table_hard to every rule kind, numbers to 100, three rows out of order, find the rule then Check. Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing.
teaches: Use and find the rule of an input-output table (3.OA.D.9 arithmetic patterns, 4.OA.C.5 generate a pattern that follows a given rule, 5.OA.B.3; EE M.EE.3.OA.8, M.EE.4.OA.5). Owner's lessons: #5 'Find the rule in an input-output table' (Y4 links, G3, W05: ftTask rule, + / - to 100 and x / / to 20) and #20 'Follow a given rule to extend a number pattern' (Y5 links, G4, W09: related, ftTask outputs with + / -).
research: From repo sources: the owner's sample sheet ('Find the rule for each function table', 'Complete each function table', 2026-09-25, gen-function-table.js header), EXTENSION_PLAYBOOK 4.15 PF-M3 / PF-M5, the detailed lesson g3-oa9-input-output-rule (its research section 4), data/curriculum/links/Y4.json and Y5.json notes. MW4K / IXL not opened this round (budget); the design standards outrank them.
problemTypes: outputs: the rule is given (machine box), the In numbers printed, write each Out (the worked column 'n + 7' beside each In prints on Model / first Guided rows only: a hint that fades)

rule: every row printed; write the rule as a sign in a circle and a number in a box (two pairs for a two-step rule), in the machine's box at S / M, under the table where the machine row would not fit a third of the page
inputs: the rule is given, the Out numbers printed, write each In (the rule worked backward)
mixed: each row has one blank, some In and some Out
make: the rule is given and a note says which In numbers to use; the pupil chooses the In numbers and writes their Outs (any rows that follow the rule are right)
-check: one more In number in a Check row under (or beside) the table; write its Out
progression: outputs with + / - to 20 (easy default) -> outputs with x / / to 20 (table facts) -> inputs (backward) -> mixed -> rule (+ / - to 100, then x / / to 20, lesson #5) -> rule with a first row that fits two rules (ftTrap) -> two-step rules (x then +) -> make your own

one change a step (P-1): the task, the rule kind or the number size changes, never two at once; the worked column and the machine picture are the hint scaffolds that fade (support frame -> frame-bare -> line -> line-bare)

drawing.sizes: XP-D-15: heavy outer rule, hairline inner rules, heavy rule under the head row, head row bold on the single grey (white when photocopy-safe). Row height Hw + 4 mm (10 / 12 / 14 mm S / M / L); every writing box at least 14 / 14 / 16 mm wide and the same width in every blank (no length leak); numbers at the digit size, heads and rule text at the text size. The machine: 'In', a 4.5 mm arrow, a heavy box, a 4.5 mm arrow, 'Out', 1 mm gaps. Footprint 56 x 61 mm at S (outputs, 4 rows), 55 x 62 mm find-the-rule at S (frame in the machine), 56 x 81 / 56 x 93 mm at L.
notes: Capacity: Independent / test page, 4-row tables: S 9 (3 x 3), M 9, L 6 (3 x 2) for outputs, inputs, mixed and rule (rule at S / M with the frame in the machine). A Check row or a 5-row table is a bigger drawing: S 6, L 4 (skill-options addsDrawingValues).

payload: {task, rule [{op, n}], rows [{x, y, hide: null|in|out|both}], check {x, y}|null, support frame|line, machine bool, note?, trap?}; slots in reading order r<i>in / r<i>out, s0 n0 [s1 n1] (frame) or rule (line), chk; q.ans joins them ', '.
find the rule: exactly one rule of the rule space (+k, -k, xk, /k, xa +/- b, /a +/- b) fits the rows (rulesFitting === 1), so + and x can never both be right; at least three rows.
Numbers to N (band) caps EVERY number in the table, the rule's own numbers and the Check row included; Max Number lowers it only when set below the band (pvCap). Division is always exact.
Key (AK-1): the same table with every blank written; a make table shows one right set and accepts any rows that follow the rule on screen.
Lesson (detailed g3-oa9-input-output-rule and the packet): the anchor chart's step states write the tried rule in the machine's box (machineText), so the chart never puts the frame in the box.

ruleGroups.title: Key and the one answer place (quoted)

ownerRulings.ruling: Function tables from the owner's sample sheet: 'Find the rule for each function table' and 'Complete each function table' (In (x) | x + 7 | Out), rebuilt as one kit cell and extended: missing In numbers, mixed blanks, make your own, a function-machine header, a Check row, a rule frame that fades to a line, In numbers out of order.

Lesson #5 (Y4 links, G3, W05, 3.OA.D.9): function_table_easy {ftTask: rule} with + / - rules to 100 and x / / rules with EVERY number to 20, so every row is a table fact (x 2 to x 5, / 2 to / 5); two-step rules left out at W05.
ownerRulings.source: owner's BUILD lesson list, data/curriculum/links/Y4.json note

ownerRulings.ruling: Lesson #20 (Y5 links, G4, W09, 4.OA.C.5): function_table_easy {ftTask: outputs, ftRules: [+, -]} is the related skill: the same given rule applied to each In number.
Top of the box is the default (CL-4b); content never shrinks to fit; one answer place per answer (VQ-2).
F1 The rule is written IN the machine box at S and M, under the table at L (one rule place).
F2 × 6 is allowed on 3-row tables at band 20 for lesson #5 (the rows are table facts; ftFactors restricts).
F3 Check rows and 5-row tables count as adding a drawing (options-render capacity).
F4 Two-step rules stay offered on function_table_easy, off by default.
Every PROPOSED decision of section 7a is accepted as written.

misconceptions.error: adds instead of multiplies: reads the rule off one row as the gap (add-for-times)
reads down the Out column, not across the row: the gap between neighbouring Outs (neighbour-outputs)
misconceptions.wrong: Outs 6, 9, 12: writes + 3 for a x 3 table

misconceptions.error: uses the rule backwards: does the rule forward to an Out to find its In (backwards)
applies the rule twice: to the In and then to the Out (rule-on-output)
sign flipped: + when the Out is smaller (sign-flip)

options: Every option is read by gen-function-table.js (ftOptions); the five panel controls (Task, Rules, Numbers to, Table, Support) plus ftTrap and ftFactors (lesson 5). Old ids fold on decode (_ftFold).
addsDrawingValues (lf-algebra r1): ftTask *-check and ftTable 51 / 52 add a drawing (the Check row, a fifth row), so a page of them may hold fewer tables.
Preset skills: algebra:function_table_find_rule {ftTask: rule}, algebra:function_table_find_inputs {ftTask: inputs} (skill-presets.js).
